body:
The v0.2.9 Lean-only migration exposes native capacity differences and leaves ten historical stress tests explicitly ignored. Restore meaningful native capacity coverage and resolve or explicitly review the changed admission limits. This is more than the process-startup latency measured in #274: some formerly expected-success programs now exhaust native work or time out before reaching their expected export/diagnostic checks.

**Affected:** unpublished v0.2.9 migration workspace, observed 2026-10-03, macOS arm64, Rust 1.98.1, Lean 4.30.0. **Target: v0.3.1**, explicitly requested by the maintainer; label `0.3.1 TODO`. This issue does not reintroduce a Rust verifier or postpone the approved Lean-only architecture in #276.

## Evidence and scope

The retained broad run completed 72 targets with 574 tests passing, two failing and 49 ignored. Its two remaining failures in `review_v020` were:

- `many_receipts_round_trip_shared_source_without_repeated_storage_work`: `function semantic contract: native function checking exceeded its bounded profile`.
- `capacity_diagnostics_identify_the_declaration_and_exact_arithmetic_limit`: `limit: Lean native checker timed out; no fallback`, before the expected old Rust expansion diagnostic.

Earlier retained logs also show timeouts for long identity/source trajectories and the export-capacity case, plus native work-limit failures in the two 256-receipt/source-sharing tests. Some other initial failures were caused by rebuilding/replacing the checker during the run; do not count those as demonstrated semantic or capacity regressions. The raw scaling cases were already deferred, and the old maximum evidence-depth/expansion expectation needs a controlled native reproduction. **Ten ignored tests are a coverage gap, not ten independently established bugs.**

Native per-decision work is bounded at 10,000,000 units, with a shared caller budget and a 60-second process deadline. Repeated fresh decisions charge source transport again. Native JSON and combined program/evidence graph depth limits also differ from the old Rust counters. These are observed mechanisms and limits, not a completed root-cause analysis; batching alone has not been shown to fix the long-gate timeouts.

Original sources and actual logs are retained in the working tree:

- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/cutover/README.md`
- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/cutover/validation.json`
- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/cutover/logs/rust-tests.log`
- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/cutover/logs/rust-tests2.log`
- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/cutover/logs/review20-final.log`

Retained log SHA-256 values: `rust-tests.log` = `1cb3105183748509307163260fabb6c5141f0e866989a373ca972cb5080f0322`; `rust-tests2.log` = `c36f57449664b89bed55c52211cd1f1ebf643ac0ce132e553aef1d4a4d6ec92e`.

The subsequent focused `review_v020` run passed its two active tests with four historical stress tests ignored. That is not evidence that the capacity failures were fixed. Small source-binding, shared-receipt, round-trip and independent semantic tests remain active. No published release or immutable commit containing these changes is claimed.

## Retained tests to account for individually

Each item requires a recorded outcome and a disposition; removing an `ignore` or replacing a success assertion with a generic rejection is not sufficient.

- [ ] `tests/native_raw.rs::many_live_wires_do_not_require_quadratic_duplicate_checks` — 80,000 live wire owners; deferred scaling coverage.
- [ ] `tests/native_raw.rs::many_branches_share_freshness_history_without_leaking_classical_scopes` — 8,000 branches; deferred scope/freshness scaling coverage.
- [ ] `tests/function_evidence.rs::dependency_depth_and_expanded_execution_cost_are_bounded` — dependency depth and shared-DAG expansion; separate native combined-graph limits from the former Rust counters.
- [ ] `tests/interop.rs::export_has_independent_capacity_checks` — 4,097-gate and 13-qubit export limits; ensure acceptance does not prevent meaningful exporter-capacity coverage.
- [ ] `tests/review_v020.rs::long_source_trajectory_samples_with_the_original_cli_budget` — source trajectory timeout.
- [ ] `tests/review_v020.rs::long_identity_circuits_normalize_both_flat_and_compound_steps` — 12,000-gate flat/compound identity trajectories.
- [ ] `tests/review_v020.rs::many_receipts_round_trip_shared_source_without_repeated_storage_work` — shared-source receipts, QIRF1/2 round trips and added 300 KB source text.
- [ ] `tests/review_v020.rs::capacity_diagnostics_identify_the_declaration_and_exact_arithmetic_limit` — predictable bounded rejection with the relevant source declaration and useful diagnostic.
- [ ] `tests/source_snapshots.rs::full_256_specializations_survive_a_100kb_project_and_unrelated_comments` — fresh-native work charged across 256 specializations.
- [ ] `tests/source_snapshots.rs::distinct_contract_pairs_and_static_providers_share_one_project_snapshot` — source sharing across distinct receipts/providers.

## Reproduction and validation policy

Do not run all ignored tests indiscriminately. Current contributor instructions restrict validation to small systems and prohibit newly running maximum-size cases. Start by reducing the recorded failures to bounded reproductions, without weakening ownership, phase, tuple, source/evidence or exact-artifact binding. Run the preserved maximum cases only when the maintainer authorizes that scope.

For a later authorized stress run, build/audit the matching native checker once, keep it stable during the run, and select it explicitly. For example:

```sh
export QLEISLI_KERNEL=/absolute/path/to/audited/qleisli-kernel
cargo test --locked --offline --test review_v020 \
  many_receipts_round_trip_shared_source_without_repeated_storage_work \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

Record source/binary hashes, environment, input dimensions, elapsed time, memory where measured, reported work/diagnostics and failure class. A crash, timeout or malformed response is not a passing semantic rejection test. This tracking issue was created from retained evidence; maximum-size tests were not rerun to file it.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Isolate repeated metadata/transport work, native checking complexity, depth/profile limits and diagnostic ordering with bounded reproductions. Share implementation work with #274 without assuming startup explains every failure.
- [ ] Restore expected acceptance where required, or obtain an explicit reviewed profile/capacity decision for changed admission. Preserve the original cases and explain any replacement. Raising time/work limits alone is not a demonstrated fix; maintain finite resource bounds and the small detector policy.
- [ ] For every item above, reactivate useful automated coverage or replace it with equivalent reviewed boundary coverage and a separately controlled stress lane. Preserve independent semantic/source-binding assertions and source-localized capacity diagnostics. No unexplained permanent ignores.
- [ ] Preserve Lean-only fresh acceptance, immutable original artifact/request/source bindings, checks of unused declarations and rejection on checker failure. No Rust fallback, unchecked receipts or algorithm-specific acceptance exceptions.
- [ ] Run and record the repaired bounded regression suite and the frozen 799-pair native replay. Validate authorized stress cases with a stable audited checker before claiming stress recovery; separate deferred, failed and passed results.

Related: #276 owns the migration/release gates; #274 owns process batching and repeated metadata costs; #275 owns diagnostic classification; #94 tracks the broader organization of capacity limits. This issue owns the concrete ten-test capacity/coverage recovery. Full Soundness and resource theorems remain separate proof obligations.
title: v0.2.9 bug: resolve native capacity regressions and restore 10 deferred stress tests

body:
## Observation in v0.2.9

The independent Rust/native QIRF comparison agrees on acceptance for all **799 distinct artifact/request pairs**: **263 accepted, 536 rejected, zero acceptance disagreements**. However, **294 rejected pairs receive different diagnostic codes**:

| Rust | Lean native | Pairs |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `format` | `invalid_ir` | 289 |
| `invalid_ir` | `contract` | 5 |

The native protocol currently collapses several failure classes. Selecting a verifier can therefore change the machine-readable classification of an identical rejected input. The user requested a **bug issue observed in v0.2.9**, deferred with the **0.3.1 TODO** label. This is a diagnostic consistency issue, not an observed acceptance/soundness disagreement.

## Recorded evidence and reproduction

Measured on 2026-10-03 against the uncommitted v0.2.9 migration workspace. Both verifiers run independently on the same original QIRF/request bytes; the combined dual-checking path is not used as an oracle. A debug-CLI run matching CI and a preliminary release-CLI run gave the same 799 decisions. Coverage includes all 19 raw constructors, 84 small corpus clients plus two source fixtures, frozen QIRF1/2 artifacts, independent requests and seeded field mutations.

Evidence is retained in the v0.2.9 working tree, not yet published at a release tag:

- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/equivalence/README.md`
- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/equivalence/results.json` — SHA-256 `3b5f3bf8d5d7311114b302bfe78e3eb0ec76ef4700af6b8fe4cf339bf6d1c699`; includes source/binary hashes and each pair of decisions/codes.
- `tests/fixtures/verification_v029/equivalence/inputs.jsonl.gz` — original artifact/request bytes, names and aliases; base64 fields in JSONL.
- `scripts/test_verifier_equivalence.py` — fixed seed `2903102026`, records diagnostics separately from acceptance, fails on protocol/process errors.

```sh
cargo build --locked --offline --bin qleisli
(cd lean-kernel && lake build)
python3 scripts/test_verifier_equivalence.py --record /tmp/qleisli-diagnostics-new
```

Use a new output directory. Inspect rows where `rust.code != lean.code` in `results.json` and the corresponding original input in `inputs.jsonl.gz`.

## v0.3.1 work and acceptance

- Define and review consistent meanings for `format`, `invalid_ir`, `contract` and `limit` across Rust import and native QIRF/request validation, preserving the public diagnostic vocabulary.
- Preserve enough native failure information to distinguish parse/schema failures, invalid IR structure and failed semantic requirements; avoid reclassifying all failures into one generic bucket merely to obtain equality.
- Add targeted cases for both observed discrepancy classes, and extend the independent comparison to assert the reviewed diagnostic mapping as well as acceptance.
- Eliminate the 294 observed discrepancies under that mapping while retaining the 263/536 acceptance outcomes and process/protocol failure checks. Keep the original baseline intact and save a new comparison record.
- Review compatibility of any machine-readable code change before implementation. Target compatible correction in v0.3.1; any genuinely breaking public-contract change requires a separately agreed MINOR migration rather than an unannounced PATCH break.

Related: #271 addresses function-contract versus operation-contract errors in the Rust source frontend. This issue tracks the broader independently measured **Rust-versus-Lean QIRF verifier** discrepancy set; link shared classification work without replacing either regression scope. #225 tracks the diagnostic design principles.
title: v0.2.9 bug: align Rust and Lean verifier error classifications

body:
Found while writing small `.qli` programs against v0.2.8 (`18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0`). Related: #225 (keep failures distinguishable; stable codes), #112, #264.

## Problem

The closed v1 code set includes both `invalid_ir` and `contract`. Two sibling source paths classify the same kind of failure differently:

- **Function contracts:** `apply_contract` maps every non-capacity `ContractError`, including `EquationMismatch`, to `invalid_ir` ([src/frontend/compile/lower/function_contract.rs L90-L98](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/compile/lower/function_contract.rs#L90-L98)).
- **Static operation contracts:** non-capacity `ContractError`s map to `contract` ([src/frontend/compile/operations.rs L108-L112](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/compile/operations.rs#L108-L112)).

As a result, a source program whose implementation simply does not meet its specification is reported as if the compiler had produced invalid IR:

```text
main.qli:19:5: invalid_ir: function semantic contract: exact equation U E_in = E_out u does not hold; ...
```

## Suggested fix

Report semantic contract failures from `apply_contract` (equation mismatch, signature/type mismatch) as `contract`. Keep `invalid_ir` for genuinely malformed or unchecked IR, such as "contract dependency has not been independently checked" ([L74](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/compile/lower/function_contract.rs#L74)).

This changes a machine-readable code. Please decide whether it is a compatible PATCH correction or belongs to a MINOR target.

## Acceptance

- An `apply_contract` equation mismatch reports `contract` in both text and JSON output, consistent with operation contracts, with a test.
title: v0.2.8 review: function-contract equation failures report `invalid_ir`, while operation contracts report `contract`

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0`. Proposed scope: compatible PATCH robustness repair; this Issue does not select a release.

Related: #223 concerns the broader native CI harness. This issue is about the runtime process boundary of the public `--lean-kernel` adapter itself.

## Problem

The dual runtime starts the selected checker with piped stdin/stdout and separate reader/writer threads:

https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/interchange/dual/runtime.rs

The code correctly recognizes that a descendant can inherit a pipe handle:

```rust
// Do not join potentially blocked pipes after exit/timeout: a descendant
// might have inherited a handle.
```

But on timeout or any other error it only does:

```rust
let _ = child.kill();
let _ = child.wait();
```

That terminates only the direct child. A wrapper selected through `--lean-kernel=PATH` can fork/spawn a descendant that inherits stdout or stdin, exit, and leave the descendant alive. The Rust reader/writer thread is deliberately not joined, so it can remain blocked until that descendant closes its inherited handle.

The existing Unix regression includes:

```sh
sleep 4 &
exit 0
```

but it asserts only that the caller returns before the deadline. It does not assert that the background process was terminated or that no blocked transport thread remains.

## Why this matters

The audited Qleisli kernel itself does not intentionally fork, so this is not a claim about Lean soundness. It is a robustness boundary for a user-selected executable path.

Repeated checks against a broken or wrapped checker can accumulate orphan descendants and detached pipe threads. The timeout therefore bounds the API call latency but not all resources created by that call.

The native CI runner already handles the analogous problem by starting a separate session and killing the process group on timeout.

## Suggested fix

Treat each dual-check invocation as a process tree rather than a single PID.

- Unix: place the checker in a dedicated process group/session and kill the whole group on timeout/error.
- Windows: use an equivalent Job Object / process-tree mechanism where available.
- Keep the strict stdout framing and no-fallback behavior unchanged.

The cleanup path should also ensure transport threads cannot remain indefinitely blocked on descendants created by that invocation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Add a regression in which the checker spawns a long-lived descendant that inherits stdout and then exits or stalls.
- [ ] After timeout/failure, the descendant is no longer alive.
- [ ] No reader/writer thread from the failed invocation remains blocked on an inherited pipe.
- [ ] A successful ordinary checker invocation is unaffected.
- [ ] Existing malformed-response, oversized-response, failed-status and timeout regressions continue to pass.
title: v0.2.8 review: dual-checker timeout kills only the direct child and can leave descendants behind

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0`. Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

Related: #131 discusses future frontend/root architecture, but this is a concrete v0.2.8 CLI regression in the current finite frontend.

## Problem

Plain `qleisli check` intentionally supports library roots without `main::main`:

- `check_project_with_policy` calls the common project processor with `require_entry = false`.
- Its documentation explicitly says it checks every declaration, including library roots with no entry function.

Source:
https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/compile/mod.rs

The new dual path changes that behavior. In `source_commands::execute`:

```rust
if options.command == "check" && options.lean_kernel.is_none() {
    // check-only path: no entry required
    ...
}

let program = match &options.selected_root {
    Some(selected) => selected.compile_with_policy(options.policy)?,
    None => compile_project_with_policy(root, options.policy)?,
};
...
if options.command == "check" {
    return Ok(Success::Checked);
}
```

Source:
https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli/source_commands.rs

Both compile paths use `require_entry = true`. Therefore adding `--lean-kernel=PATH` to a valid mainless library check changes the source acceptance path from "check every declaration" to "compile required entry" and fails with `invalid_entry` before dual verification.

The VM-28 regression uses a project with an entry point, so it does not cover this difference.

## Why this matters

`--lean-kernel` is presented as an opt-in additional Rust/Lean acceptance gate. It should not accidentally change `check` into `compile` or silently narrow the source-language domain through an unrelated entry-point requirement.

If the current QIRF dual protocol fundamentally cannot represent a library-only check, that should be an explicit documented boundary rather than an accidental `invalid_entry` produced by reusing the compile path.

## Suggested fix

Separate "check all declarations" from "obtain an executable root program for dual verification".

Possible designs include:

- extend the dual protocol to represent/check library-root obligations; or
- preserve ordinary `check` semantics and explicitly specify what dual verification means when no executable root exists.

Whichever design is chosen, do not implement it by silently routing `check` through `compile_project_with_policy`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Add a mainless library fixture that succeeds under ordinary `qleisli check`.
- [ ] Exercise the same fixture with `--lean-kernel` in text and JSON modes.
- [ ] The result follows an explicitly documented dual-check contract and does not fail merely because the source path was routed through `require_entry = true`.
- [ ] Existing entry-bearing dual `check/run/sample/emit-ir` regressions continue to pass.
- [ ] `--qrate` and non-`--qrate` library roots have the same documented behavior.
title: v0.2.8 review: `check --lean-kernel` accidentally requires an entry point

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0`. Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

Related: #192 fixed the persistent `[source].root` replacement race by retaining a directory identity. This is a residual ABA form: the pathname can be temporarily replaced during loading and restored before the post-load identity check.

## Problem

`QrateSource` retains the originally selected directory handle, but loading is still driven by the pathname:

- `QrateSource::unchanged()` reopens `self.root` and compares its Unix `(dev, ino)` to the held directory.
- `QrateSource::load_with_policy()` checks `unchanged()`, calls `Project::load_resolved(&self.root, ...)`, then checks `unchanged()` again.
- `Project::load_resolved` reacquires the root by pathname and source discovery/reads continue from pathname-based traversal rather than from the held `QrateSource.directory` identity.

Sources:
- https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project/manifest.rs
- https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project.rs
- https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project/source_file.rs

This closes a persistent replacement, but not an ABA replacement:

```text
A = originally selected source directory

pre-check: pathname -> A, identity matches held A
           |
           +-- rename/swap pathname to B
load:      pathname-based discovery/read uses B
           +-- restore pathname -> A
post-check: pathname -> A, identity matches held A
```

Both identity checks pass even though source bytes may have been loaded from B.

The existing v0.2.8 replacement regressions leave the replacement in place through the post-check, so they do not cover this transient swap/restore case.

## Why this matters

The purpose of #192 was to bind `--qrate` loading to the source root that was actually selected. A pre/post pathname identity comparison is not enough to establish that the bytes read between those checks came from that identity.

This is not a claim of a filesystem snapshot against ordinary concurrent writes. The narrower requirement is that source discovery and reads remain rooted in the selected directory identity instead of a replaceable pathname.

## Suggested fix

Use the retained directory handle as the actual traversal anchor for source discovery and file opening, rather than only as an identity witness.

On Unix, descriptor-relative traversal from the held root is the natural model. Other platforms can use the strongest corresponding directory-handle semantics available. Avoid a design that merely adds more pathname checks around pathname-based reads.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Add a deterministic regression with synchronization that temporarily replaces the selected root after the first identity check, allows loading to proceed from the replacement, then restores the original root before the final check.
- [ ] The transient replacement is rejected, and no source from the replacement tree is accepted.
- [ ] Persistent replacement and replacement-symlink regressions from #192 continue to pass.
- [ ] Ordinary non-symlink `--qrate` loading remains unchanged.
- [ ] The guarantee is stated as selected-root identity binding, not a snapshot guarantee for concurrent writes to already selected regular files.
title: v0.2.8 review: `QrateSource` pre/post identity checks allow transient ABA root replacement

Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

`Circuit::validate` ([src/contract/mod.rs L239-L272](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/contract/mod.rs#L239-L272)) returns `ContractError::Limit` when a step has:

- more controls than register bits;
- more contract axes than register bits;
- permutation or phase tables longer than 2^bits.

No valid circuit can have these shapes, because axes and controls must be distinct and in range; `check_circuit` would reject them as `InvalidCircuit`. But `ContractError::is_capacity` treats every `Limit` as a capacity failure ([L51-L61](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/contract/mod.rs#L51-L61)). As a result:

- `verify` sets `limit_failure` ([src/verify.rs L295](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/verify.rs#L295)).
- QIRF import reports code `limit` instead of `invalid_ir` ([src/interchange/mod.rs L740-L746](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/interchange/mod.rs#L740-L746)).
- Function-evidence checking reports that verification "exceeded its work budget or finite capacity" ([src/contract/function.rs L185-L193](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/contract/function.rs#L185-L193)).

## Scenario (derived from the code; not yet reproduced)

A QIRF artifact contains a `CertifiedCompute` on a 1-bit source (2 physical bits including the computed bit), with a use step that has 3 controls. It is rejected with code `limit` rather than `invalid_ir`. The artifact is still rejected; only the classification and message are wrong.

## Suggested fix

Keep the early bounds, since they protect traversal, but return `InvalidCircuit` for shapes that cannot fit the register. Reserve `Limit` for genuine capacity bounds such as `MAX_CONTRACT_STEPS`.

## Acceptance

- Impossible shapes yield `invalid_ir` / `InvalidCircuit`, with a test; true capacity overruns still yield `limit`.
title: v0.2.8 review: structurally invalid contract circuits are classified as capacity limits

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

`render_markdown` concatenates every item into one Markdown document. `render_source` fences signatures safely ([src/frontend/documentation.rs L183-L192](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/documentation.rs#L183-L192)). Doc-comment text, however, is copied verbatim ([L171-L181](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/documentation.rs#L171-L181)), between headings emitted at [L155-L159](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/documentation.rs#L155-L159).

An unterminated code fence, an HTML block or `<!--` in one item's doc comment, even on a private item, therefore changes how every later `## name (public)` heading and signature renders.

## Reproduction (observed)

In a probe, a private function's doc comment ended with an unterminated ```` ``` ```` line. In the `qleisli doc` output, the next public `observe fn` heading and its ```` ```qli ```` signature fence were rendered inside that open code block, so the public declaration was hidden or garbled. An unterminated `<!--` in a private helper's doc similarly hides every later declaration in rendered HTML.

## Suggested fix

Render each item's documentation in isolation: close any open fence or HTML block at the end of each item, or escape or fence the doc text, so one item cannot affect later ones.

## Acceptance

- A test with an unterminated fence and an unterminated `<!--` in one item's doc still renders every later heading and signature.
title: v0.2.8 review: `qleisli doc` lets one item's doc comment swallow later headings and signatures

Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

Related: #242 fixed the same problem for `qleisli interop`. The `--lean-kernel` dual checker added in v0.2.8 brings it back in the main CLI.

## Problem

The closed v1 diagnostic codes are fixed in [machine-interface-spec.md L9](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/7844a10d63880a2b6984c093e2dc7a75033d1e1e/docs/machine-interface-spec.md?plain=1#L9). The dual runtime reports every transport failure as `Error::new("io", ...)`:

- [src/interchange/dual.rs L64](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/interchange/dual.rs#L64)
- [src/interchange/dual/runtime.rs L64-L117](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/interchange/dual/runtime.rs#L64-L117), [L187](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/interchange/dual/runtime.rs#L187), [L218](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/interchange/dual/runtime.rs#L218)

The JSON CLI passes `error.code` through unchanged ([src/bin/qleisli/json.rs L191](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli/json.rs#L191), [L250-L252](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli/json.rs#L250-L252)).

## Reproduction (observed)

```sh
qleisli check examples/bell --format=json --lean-kernel=/nonexistent-kernel
```

The output is a `qleisli.result` v1 envelope whose diagnostic has `"code":"io"`, and the exit status is 1.

## Suggested fix

Map dual-checker transport failures to a code in the closed set, as #242 did with `project` for interop I/O, or version the addition. Add a test that every JSON CLI failure code, including `--lean-kernel` failures, belongs to the closed set.

## Acceptance

- `--lean-kernel` failures in `check`, `run`, `sample`, `emit-ir` and `verify-ir` use closed-set codes, and a test enforces it.
title: v0.2.8 review: `--lean-kernel` failures emit diagnostic code `io` outside the closed v1 set

Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

`sample` and `doc` write with `write_all` and turn write errors into a diagnostic and exit 1 ([src/bin/qleisli.rs L102-L107](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli.rs#L102-L107), [L135-L140](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli.rs#L135-L140)). The other success paths use `println!`, which panics on a write error such as `EPIPE`, because Rust ignores `SIGPIPE`. Affected paths:

- `emit-ir` ([L76](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli.rs#L76))
- `verify-ir` ([L80](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli.rs#L80))
- `check` ([L117](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli.rs#L117))
- `run` ([L149](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli.rs#L149))
- the sized command ([src/bin/qleisli/sized.rs L232](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/bin/qleisli/sized.rs#L232))

## Reproduction (observed)

```sh
(qleisli run examples/bell) | (exec 0<&-; true)
```

This panics with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe` and exits 101. Under the same pipe, `qleisli sample examples/bell --shots=3 --seed=1` exits 1 with `could not write sample results`. `emit-ir` has already written its artifact, but the process still reports a panic.

## Suggested fix

Route all stdout output through the same `write_all` handling that `sample` and `doc` use.

## Acceptance

- With stdout closed, every text-mode command exits 1 with a diagnostic and does not panic, with a test.
title: v0.2.8 review: text-mode CLI output panics with exit 101 when stdout is closed

Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

`--qrate` source-root selection rejects a `target` component using a byte-exact comparison ([src/frontend/project/manifest.rs L113-L115](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project/manifest.rs#L113-L115)). It then resolves the path with `fs::symlink_metadata` ([L116-L120](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project/manifest.rs#L116-L120)). On case-insensitive filesystems (the macOS APFS default, Windows NTFS), `root = "TARGET"`, `"Target"` or `"src/TARGET"` resolves to the real `target/` build directory.

## Reproduction (observed on macOS APFS)

The qrate contains `target/main.qli` and a `Qargo.toml` with `[source] root = "TARGET"`. `QrateSource::select` returns `.../TARGET`, and `load_with_policy(SourcePolicy::default())` succeeds. `--qrate` therefore checks and runs build-directory contents that manifest validation is meant to forbid.

## Suggested fix

Compare case-insensitively (e.g. `eq_ignore_ascii_case("target")`), or compare the canonicalized selected directory with the canonical `root/target`.

## Acceptance

- `root = "TARGET"` and other mixed-case variants, including as later path components, are rejected with the existing diagnostic, with a test.
title: v0.2.8 review: `[source].root` target-directory exclusion is bypassed by letter case on case-insensitive filesystems

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

The bounded `SourcePolicy` charges only source bytes ([src/frontend/project.rs L86-L112](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project.rs#L86-L112)). For every `.qli` file, project loading calls `edition::check_directory(parent)` ([L368-L371](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project.rs#L368-L371)). `collect_qli_files` makes the same call for every `.qlt` file ([L604-L607](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project.rs#L604-L607)).

Each `check_directory` call walks up to the enclosing manifest, reads up to 64 KiB and runs a full TOML parse, with no cache ([src/frontend/project/edition.rs L34-L50](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/frontend/project/edition.rs#L34-L50)). Empty files use none of the byte budget, and the number of files and directory entries is not bounded.

## Reproduction (observed, release build on macOS)

The project contains a valid ~60 KB `Qargo.toml`, `main.qli` and 2,000 empty `.qli` files. `Project::load_with_policy(root, SourcePolicy::default())` took 8.46 s, versus 0.14 s with a 44-byte manifest (about 4.2 ms per empty file). At 50,000 files this becomes minutes of CPU while using 0 bytes of the 16 MiB project budget.

## Suggested fix

Within one load, check each manifest once per directory or per resolved manifest path. Add a file-count or directory-entry limit to the bounded policy, or charge a fixed cost per file.

## Acceptance

- Each manifest is read and parsed at most once per load.
- A test shows the bounded policy rejects a project that exceeds the file-count limit.


## Relationship to #191

#191 tracks the older per-invocation duplicate manifest reads/parses. This issue extends the same cache/resolution concern to per-source-file loading and separately adds a missing file-count/resource bound.
title: v0.2.8 review: source loading re-parses Qargo.toml for every source file and does not bound file count

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

`SimulationLimits::max_amplitude_cells` is documented as "Total complex amplitudes retained across all ensemble components" ([src/sim.rs L35-L36](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/sim.rs#L35-L36)). However, `execute_ops` ([src/sim.rs L492-L517](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/sim.rs#L492-L517)) counts only the successors of the current operation (`next_cells` and `next.len()`).

A `ClassicalBranch` runs its selected arm through a recursive `execute_ops(vec![component], arm, ...)` ([src/sim.rs L444-L458](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/sim.rs#L444-L458)) with fresh accounting. While the arm runs, the caller still holds two sets of components that the inner check does not count:

- its not-yet-processed components, inside the `for component in ensemble` iterator;
- the successors already pushed to its `next`.

`max_components` has the same gap.

## Scenario (derived from the code; not yet reproduced)

1. Grow the ensemble to the limit, e.g. 16 components × 2^16 cells = 2^20.
2. Reach a `ClassicalBranch`. The first component enters the arm while the other 15 stay alive.
3. Inside the arm, grow to the limit again and branch again.

The verifier allows 64 levels of branch nesting, so retained amplitudes can reach about 64× `max_amplitude_cells`. With the default 16 MiB limit, that is about 1 GiB of `Complex` values. The step budget does not stop this, because each level needs only on the order of 100 IR visits.

## Suggested fix

Thread one ensemble-wide account through the recursion: the cells and components currently retained, including the caller's pending components. Alternatively, execute branches iteratively over the whole ensemble so that one check covers everything retained.

## Acceptance

- A nested-branch regression test that exceeds `max_amplitude_cells` only when counted across levels is rejected with `AmplitudeLimit`. A similar test covers `max_components`.
title: v0.2.8 review: simulation amplitude/component limits are checked per branch level, not across the retained ensemble

body:
Found in the v0.2.8 code review of the published source `18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0` (`src/` is unchanged on `main` at `059833c`). Proposed scope: compatible PATCH repair; this Issue does not select a release.

## Problem

`Component::project_remove` ([src/sim/state.rs L135-L158](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/sim/state.rs#L135-L158)) deep-clones both `tokens` and the whole `classical: BTreeMap<ClassicalId, bool>` for every outcome component it creates. `MeasureZ`, `Reset` and `Discard` all use it ([src/sim.rs L374-L420](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/sim.rs#L374-L420)). Classical values are never removed from the map. Once K components exist, memory is O(K × C) for C classical values, and each projection costs O(C).

`SimulationLimits` bounds none of this ([src/sim.rs L32-L40](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/18020190b1c80037442be29d74e90fd9e07253e0/src/sim.rs#L32-L40)). `max_amplitude_cells` counts amplitudes, `max_components` counts components, and `max_execution_steps` counts IR visits. A projection is charged as one step regardless of C.

## Scenario (derived from the code; not yet reproduced)

Consider a closed, verifiable `observe` program, for example an imported QIRF artifact: 20,000 `ClassicalConst`, then 16 × (`Init0`; `H`) and 16 `MeasureZ`.

- Steps: about 20,000 + 32 + 65,535 IR visits, under the default 1,000,000.
- Amplitude cells: at most 65,536, under the default 2^20.
- Components: 65,536, within the default.

Each of the 65,536 final components still holds its own ~20,000-entry map. That is about 1.3 × 10^9 entries, tens of GB, and no limit fires first. `sample_closed` follows one trajectory, so its memory stays bounded, but it still copies C entries per measurement (O(C × M) work per shot).

## Suggested fix

Share classical state between components, e.g. with `Arc` plus copy-on-write or a persistent map. Alternatively, charge cloned entries to the execution budget or a new limit, so `SimulationLimits` actually bounds memory and time.

## Acceptance

- Under default limits, a regression test with many classical values followed by many measurements either fails cleanly with a limit error or completes in bounded memory.
title: v0.2.8 review: simulator copies every classical value per measurement outcome, outside SimulationLimits
Bug: verification, producer, transport, and execution limits are scattered as untyped constants
